races.name: Broughton Transport The Mane Logistics Choice Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Early Release
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 6f on Firm and returns after 50 days off, but is a natural hold-up horse whose race-winning move depends on securing a clear passage late — in this compressed field that run may not materialise cleanly, and the 50-day absence adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: Strong record on Good ground (3W3P from 10 runs) is the headline angle here; Charlie Tucker claims 7lbs which helps offset the OR, and although this horse prefers to come from off the pace it has the best similar-going profile in the field.

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams has a solid 14-day strike rate and this horse has been consistently placed in recent starts, though its true role is as a rear-to-midfield finisher — the crowded hold-up pool in this race means it is unlikely to find the clear air it needs to produce its best.

runners_data.name: Grey Horizon
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and can dictate terms entirely unchallenged at this 5½f trip; the visor is noted, the trainer has only 1 winner from 12 in 14 days, and the [STYLE_FIT] flag is worth monitoring if the visor leads to a more exuberant display than ideal early.

runners_data.name: In The City
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex sends out a 47-day returner, but In The City's prominent style suits this race shape perfectly — the horse can sit second to Grey Horizon, travel into the race, and has strong Good-ground form (1W2P from 3 runs on similar surface), making it one of the most naturally positioned horses in this field.

runners_data.name: Saucy Jane
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Good ground recently and shapes as a hold-up type who, given the pace scenario, may find herself able to travel closer than usual — tongue tie (p) is noted, and the 14-day turnaround for Jack Morland (2W from 7 recent runners) keeps her in the picture.

runners_data.name: Reality Queen
runners_data.note: Liam Wright partners the lowest-weighted runner in the field; Michael Appleby fires runners regularly (4W from 35 in 14 days) and the OR-60 means she carries least weight, but her natural style places her at the rear and the redistribution into a midfield cluster makes her hard to trust unless traffic clears sharply in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Grey Horizon is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push them, Christian Howarth can dictate terms from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 5½f on good ground at Bath. In The City is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely sit second, meaning the early fractions are unlikely to be truly testing. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Early Release, Merrimack, and Reality Queen are all genuine closers who are unlikely to secure their preferred rear berth and will be shuffled into a midfield bunch, compromising their ability to produce a clean late run. A controlled pace set by Grey Horizon with a compressed midfield group behind favours the horse that can travel prominently, get a clear run off the final bend, and sustain their effort to the line — making the prominent/tracking profile the dominant tactical advantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Grey Horizon Controls Freely
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Horizon is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the gates and sets a measured pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Grey Horizon dictates every yard at a comfortable tempo, and with no genuine pace rival to force the issue, the race turns into a test of who can pick up off a steady gallop in the final furlong and a half. Horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream — In The City and Saucy Jane — are best placed to respond and hold the hold-up brigade at bay.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough to compress the field and the hold-up horses find cleaner passages than expected in the straight.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian gallop means the race is only truly run in the final furlong, and if Saucy Jane or Safari Dream manage to get a clear run without traffic issues, they can cut down the leader late. Safari Dream's strong Good-ground record and Saucy Jane's recent win at the trip give them each a foothold if the race sets up for finishing speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Horizon goes too fast for the conditions and ties up in the final 100 yards, opening the door for tracking types.
scenarios.body: Should the pace prove stronger than expected early — perhaps forced by In The City pressing hard — Grey Horizon's effort may hollow out approaching the final furlong, gifting the race to a horse sitting just off the pace. In The City, already prominent, is ideally positioned to pick up the pieces, while Saucy Jane from just off the pace could swoop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Issues Scramble Result
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield group causes significant interference in the straight, producing an unlikely winner from the rear.
scenarios.body: With three genuine hold-up types forced into a bunched midfield, a messy passage through the field could open a late gap for a horse with acceleration — Merrimack's recent consistency and form on Good ground gives it an outside claim if it finds daylight. Reality Queen, lightly weighted and with a previous win on Firm, could sneak into frame if the bunching creates an opening down the rail.

watchPoints.text: Grey Horizon's uncontested lead is the pivotal factor — watch whether Christian Howarth dictates a truly controlled tempo or allows the pace to inflate, as that single decision shapes every other runner's chance.

The three redistributed hold-up types (Early Release, Merrimack, Reality Queen) will be jostling for the same midfield ground — watch for a bunched, traffic-heavy straight that could compromise all three simultaneously.

In The City returns after 47 days and its last run is unknown (listed as "?") — watch how Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) positions it from the gate, as its race hinges entirely on a clean prominent pitch from the start.

Safari Dream's 7lb claim for Charlie Tucker is significant at this level — watch whether the weight allowance translates to a genuine competitive advantage over the 71-rated horses carrying 138lbs, particularly late in the race on Good ground where this horse has thrived.

Grey Horizon wears a visor — watch whether headgear produces a more forward-going display than its Prominent tag suggests, which could either tighten its hold on the race or burn through its reserves too early.

races.name: Resolution Canter Cup EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bellatina
runners_data.note: Has consistent placed form in 5f good-ground races (two seconds at Bath already) and Charlie Johnston's stable is in solid form at 14 days; however, her true racing style is hold-up and she is operating closer to the pace than ideal in this shape, which tempers confidence despite her course-and-distance profile being the strongest in the field.

runners_data.name: Dissenter
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's lightly raced filly with a single run over 6f on firm going behind her — the drop to 5f is untested and the going shift is a question, but Tregoning's yard sends out few runners and their lightly raced types often arrive ready; the unknown style profile means she could slot prominently and prove well above OR=120 on debut data.

runners_data.name: Last Dandelion
runners_data.note: Four runs at 6f on good and standard going without a win or place and she prefers to come from behind — the switch to 5f is a shortening of trip she hasn't tried, and the reality is she will likely find herself in a pace cluster rather than operating as the pure hold-up horse she is by inclination.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Ardad
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's filly showed a useful second at 6f on good going and now drops in trip to 5f for the first time; her hold-up style is her natural preference and she'll need pace to be injected somewhere in the race — a clean passage and a moderate tempo in the final furlong suit her best.

runners_data.name: Sheer Beauty
runners_data.note: Julia & Shelley Birkett's filly has a single run — sixth on good going at 5f — which is this exact trip and going combination, providing useful baseline form; Dylan Hogan takes the ride and her style is unknown, meaning she could be a forward-going type who benefits from the likely slow tempo if she can establish position early.

runners_data.name: Space Dreamer
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster sends out Space Dreamer 44 days after a fifth-place debut at 5f on good going — the yard is active at 14 days and Charles Bishop is an experienced sprint hand; she has seen a 5f good-ground race before which is a small but genuine advantage, and unknown style means she could press forward and exploit a drifting tempo.

runners_data.name: Tricky Jenny
runners_data.note: Three runs without reaching the frame on stand, good, and soft going — primarily a hold-up type by style but displaced into midfield here because of the density of similar-style runners; Luke Morris won't be able to find the rear he'd want, and Tricky Jenny's form at 5f is her best effort (fifth), though still uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Yankeedoodledandy
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes — both career starts have seen her beaten into eighth and thirteenth — and with only 11 days between runs, the likelihood of improvement here is slim; Taylor Fisher inherits a very difficult ride and this profile is the least suited to any scenario in this race.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field and three genuine hold-up types (Bellatina, Last Dandelion, Tricky Jenny) redistributed into midfield because the map cannot place them all at the rear, this 5f Bath maiden is likely to lack a genuine pace-setter and drift into a bunched, sprint-finish affair where position off the break becomes decisive. The three unraced fillies — Dissenter, Space Dreamer, and Sheer Beauty — carry unknown style profiles and could naturally drift forward or tuck in, making the early shape highly uncertain; Yankeedoodledandy, flagged for fading in finishes, offers little forward momentum from her dismal recent form. The field holds more hold-up horses than can realistically operate from their natural position, meaning Bellatina, Last Dandelion, and Tricky Jenny are all likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than they would prefer given how the race is likely to set up — the one who best compromises their position may benefit most. This race shape most strongly favours a horse with tactical versatility or natural pace who can travel prominently or make an early move, as a slow or drifting tempo will punish pure hold-up reliance and reward whoever hits the front with momentum in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Drift, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no runner asserts early and the pace is pedestrian, turning the final 2f into a flat-out dash.
scenarios.body: The field fans out in the closing stages with no horse able to truly quicken clear from a slow tempo, putting a premium on raw speed and a clean run; any of the lightly-raced unexposed fillies with natural pace — Dissenter or Space Dreamer — could produce a sharp debut burst that a field of hold-up types cannot match.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Filly Bolts Up
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or once-raced fillies (Dissenter, Sheer Beauty, Space Dreamer) produces a significantly better run than their bare form suggests.
scenarios.body: An unexposed filly with a strong trial or a powerful stable debut produces a performance beyond what the limited form shows, travelling prominently and asserting from 1f out; Bath's tight 5f rewards horses that jump well and sustain pace through the turns, and a filly with class to burn won't need a set-up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Catches All Napping
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast early — perhaps set by an unraced filly going hard — and the hold-up horses get a strong enough tempo to finish through.
scenarios.body: Bellatina, who has shown consistent placed form on similar going and has the best recent experience in the group, is best placed to benefit if she can get a clear run from her mapped midfield position; however, this scenario is discounted because the three redistributed hold-up types are racing out of role and may not get the strong pace needed to produce a finishing run on a track that doesn't overly favour closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Total Chaos, Outsider Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down completely — slow early, no rhythm, scrimmaging — and an unconsidered runner profits from a serendipitous passage.
scenarios.body: Sayidah Ardad, who has shown a second-place finish at 6f on good going and drops to 5f, could benefit from a chaotic race if she finds cover and a gap late; Tricky Jenny's modest form offers little encouragement but in a race with no true pace-setter anything is possible.

watchPoints.text: Dissenter and Space Dreamer are both lightly raced unknowns whose style profiles are unconfirmed — if either shows natural forward pace from the gates they could dictate the tempo and prove well above maiden class without the form book giving any warning.

Bellatina's best chance depends on getting closer to the pace than her natural hold-up style allows — watch how Sean D Bowen places her in the first furlong, because if she settles too far back in a slow-run race she may not produce her finishing effort in time over 5f.

Yankeedoodledandy is flagged as a fader and returns just 11 days after her last run — if she goes forward early and sets any kind of tempo before emptying, it could create a false pace that disrupts the shape for the hold-up horses behind her.

With Going listed as Unknown at Bath, any late ground change or watering adjustment could shift the balance toward or away from horses with soft-ground or firm-ground form — Bellatina's soft-going second and Tricky Jenny's soft record are worth monitoring against final going confirmation.

races.name: Home Group Financial Wealth Management Trophy Handicap Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old with a win over course and distance on good ground — the key piece of form in this field — though John Gallagher's stable is out of form (0 from 6 in 14 days) and the hold-up style means it is reliant on something going wrong for the leader; visor worn.|

runners_data.name: Darkened Edge
runners_data.note: The race's only natural front-runner with a recent three-from-seven strike rate for Christopher Mason's yard and a win at this trip on good ground last time; its style fit score of 0.91 reflects that it is technically mapped to prominent rather than lead here, but in practice it gets uncontested lead — that flag should be discounted given the field composition.|

runners_data.name: Little Miss Magic
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings runner carries a visor and is a natural hold-up horse with limited five-furlong form (all five recent runs at six furlongs), making this trip a concern; the crowded closer's berth means it is squeezed into a midfield position it would not naturally seek, and the trainer's 0-from-8 in 14 days adds further caution.|

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with headgear, representing Scott Dixon, who is 1 from 12 in 14 days; no wins or places from four runs on good going and zero wins or places in its full recent history makes it hard to enthuse about, though youth and light weight mean it cannot be entirely dismissed if the race falls apart.|

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Hope
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up specialist forced closer than ideal by the race's backlog of closers; going concern is p (possible concern) and the trainer Grace Harris has had a busy but low-percentage 14-day spell (2/15); the five-furlong trip on good is not its strongest combination based on recent form.|

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's second runner is a genuine hold-up horse with a couple of placed efforts at six furlongs on good ground, but the drop to five furlongs and the positional compromise make it hard to see it delivering its best; raced eight days ago and carries bottom weight alongside Symbol Of Hope, which is at least a practical advantage.|

races.paceDynamic: Darkened Edge is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner sprint and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to dictate a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front over Bath's flat five furlongs. The rest of the field — Secret Handsheikh, Little Miss Magic, Beach Partee, Symbol Of Hope, and Coast — are all hold-up types by inclination, meaning the pace is likely to be steady rather than scorching, with little natural pressure applied to Darkened Edge through the early stages. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Little Miss Magic, Symbol Of Hope, and Coast are all true closers redistributed into midfield positions on the map because they cannot all settle comfortably at the back of only six runners, and it is Beach Partee and Secret Handsheikh who are most likely to press closer to the action by default. A steady, front-runner-controlled pace on a flat, sharp track strongly favours Darkened Edge's profile — horses racing prominently with tactical control will be hardest to peg back, while genuine closers dependent on a truly-run race will find the conditions least conducive to their style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Darkened Edge Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Darkened Edge leads unchallenged at a controlled tempo, setting a pace no rival can match from the front.
scenarios.body: Darkened Edge travels kindly in front, conserving energy through the early stages before asserting from two furlongs out on the flat Bath track; with no pace pressure, it gets first run and the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up. This shape rewards the lone front-runner with tactical control, and Darkened Edge's solid five-furlong record on good ground makes it the prime beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pressed Into Faster Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one or more rivals push up closer than expected, forcing Darkened Edge into a more genuine gallop.
scenarios.body: A quicker early tempo stretches the field sooner and opens a gap for a closer to reel in a tiring leader in the final furlong; Secret Handsheikh, despite hold-up tendencies, has winning form at this course and trip and could capitalise if produced with a well-timed run. This scenario marginally improves prospects for hold-up runners, though most are redistributed from their true style and remain disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the final furlong and genuine hold-up horses arrive in time.
scenarios.body: A significant fade from the front would allow the back-markers to close, but this depends on true hold-up horses — Little Miss Magic, Coast, and Symbol Of Hope — racing from a position that suits their style, which is unlikely given the redistribution enforced by a lack of early pace. Coast has placed form at six furlongs on good ground but is conceding both distance preference and a natural tactical position here, limiting confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Muddled Race
scenarios.trigger: If traffic issues, slow starts, or positional chaos disrupt the expected order from flag to early stages.
scenarios.body: An untidy start or crowding in a compact six-runner field could scramble running positions and create a race with no clean winner on form, handing an opportunity to a lightly-weighted or well-handicapped runner finding clear daylight late. Symbol Of Hope or Beach Partee, both carrying lighter weights and without an established pattern here, represent the wildcards if chaos overrides the expected shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Darkened Edge's early lead — if it gets uncontested in front, as the pace map suggests, its rivals face a near-impossible task catching it over a flat, sharp five furlongs with no bend to bunch the field.

Watch Secret Handsheikh's early positioning — if it travels closer than its hold-up tag suggests, as course-and-distance winning form hints it might, it becomes a genuine threat to Darkened Edge in the final furlong.

Watch whether Little Miss Magic, Symbol Of Hope, or Coast can secure any meaningful position in a field of only six — all three are natural hold-up horses compressed toward midfield, and a truly slow early pace could strand them too far back to land a blow.

Watch the going closely at race time — Bath is listed as going unknown across the board, and any softening from the nominal good would shift the picture most acutely for runners with surface concerns, particularly those with headgear flagged (Secret Handsheikh, Little Miss Magic, Beach Partee).

races.name: Novacast Don't Come Last Handicap Stakes (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Man Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Veteran 10-year-old hold-up specialist with solid sim-going form (0W5P in 13 qualifying runs), best at 17-20f yet stepping back to 1m6f — if this race fails to develop into a true stamina test he loses his main edge; Neil Mulholland T14 0/8 is a concern.

runners_data.name: Assured
runners_data.note: 5-year-old with a modest recent string (557-60), lightly seen over staying trips on Good ground (0W0P in 4 qualifying runs); his natural hold-up role gets squeezed in a five-runner field where he cannot drift to the back in isolation — style fit is compromised.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: Four-year-old whose best effort is a third at 16f on Good; his true instinct is to come from the rear but with only five runners he will struggle to find space behind, limiting the effectiveness of his hold-up approach — sim-going record is modest (0W1P in 5 runs).

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old trained by the in-form Sir Mark Prescott (T14 2/12) who steps sharply up in distance from her latest second at 12f on Firm — the class edge at OR 61 stands out in this field and Morris's booking suggests an intent to be prominent rather than wait.

runners_data.name: Endofastorm
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a consistent placed record at 12f (including two seconds on Good), though his true style is hold-up and he is mapped to midfield by necessity — Kieran O'Neill takes the ride with the horse 32 days fresh, and his form at 12f may leave stamina at 1m6f unproven.

races.paceDynamic: With all five runners carrying a hold-up style rating, there is no confirmed front-runner in this 1m6f Bath contest, meaning the early stages are almost certain to be pedestrian as each jockey waits for rivals to commit. Campeona, the youngest runner and highest-rated at OR 61, is likely to be positioned with intent by Luke Morris under Sir Mark Prescott — a trainer whose 2/12 T14 record signals live form — and may be nudged forward more than her nominal style suggests. Man Of The Sea and Endofastorm both carry proven form at staying trips but will likely track the pace rather than set it, leaving the race to drift into a slow-burn contest decided by a sprint off a modest gallop in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours the horse with the most tactical versatility and finishing acceleration in a compressed finish — a profile that suits Campeona given her class edge and active trainer, while pure hold-up specialists face the risk of getting no true test of stamina to exploit. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Assured, Blue Siam, and Endofastorm are genuine hold-up horses pushed into a midfield mapping, and none of them is likely to secure a truly independent position in a field this small.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow tempo, sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field drifts along at a crawl and the race ignites only inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The absence of a genuine pacer compresses the field and turns this staying race into a flat-track sprint, with tactical sharpness and OR advantage mattering most over raw stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Campeona dictates from front
scenarios.trigger: If Luke Morris pushes Campeona forward early to fill the pace vacuum and controls the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Prescott's runners are regularly placed to exploit weak-paced fields and Campeona's OR 61 superiority means she can set a sustainable gallop and be hard to peg back from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina test grinds rivals out
scenarios.trigger: If one runner increases the tempo from halfway and the race becomes a genuine test of staying ability over the full 1m6f.
scenarios.body: Endofastorm's recent placed form at 12f on Good ground and Man Of The Sea's strong sim-going record in staying races give them the credentials to grind through it if the pace is honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers unable to land blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so muddled that hold-up horses are never able to generate momentum from the rear and get stuck in traffic.
scenarios.body: With Assured and Blue Siam both true hold-up types who cannot get their natural position in a field this size, the risk of a non-run increases markedly for both, handing the spoils to whoever is closest to the pace.

watchPoints.text: Campeona — if Luke Morris elects to fill the pace vacuum and push forward, she controls the tempo and becomes very hard to beat from the front with a significant OR advantage over the field.
Man Of The Sea — watch whether jockey Taylor Fisher attempts to manufacture a stronger gallop than usual; at 10 years old and on a 14-day turnaround, he needs a genuine stamina test to hit the frame.
Endofastorm — despite decent recent placed form, his trip history is concentrated at 12f rather than 1m6f, so a slow pace that fails to truly test stamina could expose him as the distance extends.

Blue Siam and Assured — both true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map; in a field of just five, watch how much space each jockey can actually find at the rear, as a bunched field may negate both runners' preferred tactics entirely.

races.name: Wiltshire And Bath Air Ambulance Charity Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yokkell
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two recent runs on Good going and a course-appropriate trip; trainer Wintle has a modest 14-day strike-rate, but Yokkell's sim-going figures (1W2P in 15) give him a baseline case — needs a true pace collapse to get involved from the rear in this shape.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Charm
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up mare wearing a hood, most effective over 12f and who has struggled on recent starts at this trip; sim-going figures are thin (2W5P/15) and the step back to 1m3½f from longer trips is not obviously in her favour.

runners_data.name: Bug Boy
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old whose true role is as a hold-up horse, though the field's composition means he cannot get that position cleanly; his Good-going form is limited (1W3P/15) and his last five runs have come exclusively on Soft/Good-to-Soft, making his effectiveness on drier ground a genuine question.

runners_data.name: Man Is King
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with a recent course win at a similar trip and Good going (1W2P/15 sim-going); Josephine Gordon rides and the horse wears a tongue-tie — his position in this race shape is real and natural, though the style-fit tag reflects that as a Prominent horse operating on a tight map, any significant challenge could expose him.

runners_data.name: Hope Rising
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has an outstanding record on Good going (13W+P from 15 sim-going runs) and a string of placed efforts at extended trips; Charles Bishop takes the ride for Jamie Snowden, whose yard has a positive 14-day record, and the horse's form figures suggest relentless placed consistency rather than a win breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Mark
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by inclination who is shown in midfield because of the crowded rear of the field; his best recent effort was a second on Firm going and his Good-ground figures are moderate (1W3P/15) — Zoe Hawkins's yard has had a quiet 14 days (0/3) and he needs a stronger pace than Man Is King is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Offiah's Boy
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose last five runs include poor efforts on Firm and Soft, with his best Good-going effort a 12th over 16f; Joe Tickle's yard has been active (2/13 T14) and Taylor Fisher rides, but the horse's style has been shifted out of its natural hold-up role and his form in this company does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Cezarro
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has been running over shorter trips (8-10f) and steps up in distance here; recently placed on Good going at 10f (3rd) and ran just 9 days ago, so fitness is not a concern, but the redistribution to midfield from his natural hold-up position and the lack of any win in 15 sim-going runs limits his claims materially.

races.paceDynamic: Man Is King is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 1m3½f handicap and, with no genuine rival to press him from the front, he is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish. The pace is therefore expected to be modest rather than searching, with the field strung out behind him in a relatively compressed group given the absence of pressure. Bug Boy, Jimmy Mark, Offiah's Boy and Cezarro are all true hold-up horses who have been mapped forward because the field contains more rear-runners than can realistically fill those positions — in practice, Man Is King and Hope Rising are the pair most likely to actually secure prominent berths from the draw. A steady tempo set by a single, uncontested front-runner over this distance on Good turf is a classic setup for horses that can travel prominently and pick up efficiently when the pace lifts, making prominent-to-midfield types who can quicken the favoured profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Man Is King Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Man Is King bowls along at his own pace and the field fails to close him down before the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Man Is King, with a recent win at this trip and Good going on his card, exploits a soft lead, conserves energy throughout and stretches clear when the pursuers lack the sustained finishing kick to reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If Hope Rising travels smoothly in Man Is King's slipstream and challenges from two furlongs out, turning it into a two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: Hope Rising's excellent record on Good ground and repeated placed efforts in big-field staying handicaps make her ideally suited to tracking a steady pace and grinding it out; the pair fight out a finish with the stronger stayer prevailing.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely slow and the pace only lifts very late, compressing the finish and giving hold-up horses a chance to close.
scenarios.body: Yokkell or Sea Of Charm, both proven on Good going at middle distances, could benefit if the tempo is truly pedestrian and the field bunches entering the straight; however, given the redistribution of so many genuine hold-up types to midfield, the true closers may not be ideally positioned to deliver a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Man Is King's early fractions are too fast for the conditions and he stops dramatically in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A runner like Cezarro, stepping up from shorter trips and with recent course experience, could pick up the pieces if the pace turns frantic and the front rank folds; this scenario is low-probability given Man Is King's established front-running profile and the lack of any pressuring rival.

watchPoints.text: Man Is King (Josephine Gordon) is the only natural front-runner — watch his jumping of the gates; if he misses the break or is restrained, the entire race shape dissolves and hold-up horses suddenly face a very different test.

Hope Rising has compiled a remarkable consistent run of placed efforts in similar conditions but has not won since a long absence-marker; watch whether Charles Bishop elects to press Man Is King from two furlongs out or waits — the timing of that move will likely decide the finish.

Bug Boy, Jimmy Mark and Offiah's Boy are all genuine hold-up horses competing for the same real-estate at the back of the field; if they bunch behind a slow early pace they may all block each other's runs entering the straight.

Going is listed as unknown for all six reports — Bath's watering regime can produce quick ground in summer and the actual underfoot conditions could compress or extend the decisive finishing phase; monitor any going update before race-off.

Cezarro ran just nine days ago; his fitness is an asset but watch his early behaviour under Dylan Hogan — if he jumps and races keenly over a trip beyond his recent experience, he could burn out and stop in the final quarter-mile.

races.name: Stakes Are Always High Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Havana Club
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's 4yo has shown a mix of placed efforts and poor runs recently (form: 884264), with only three runs on similar going yielding zero wins or places; a genuine hold-up type operating out of its natural rear position here, which limits its effectiveness in what is likely a modest-pace race.

runners_data.name: Blue Hero
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with one win from six recent starts, that coming over 8f on Firm ground — distance and surface are fine, but stepping back from longer trips; races from deep and has been slotted to midfield rather than the rear where it would naturally operate, complicating its ability to produce its best.

runners_data.name: Rival
runners_data.note: John & Thys Flint runner with a decent record at this trip (2nd and 4th over 8f on Good), but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 0/6 is uninspiring and the 30-day absence adds a fitness query; placed in this grade before, though its true hold-up style is obscured by the redistribution into midfield.

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: Top weight (140lbs) and highest OR (60) in the field — won over this exact course and distance on Standard going and has two further places at 8f; wears a hood and is the class benchmark here, though a trainer 14-day rate of 0/18 is a significant negative flag.

runners_data.name: My Ambition
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's 7yo was placed twice at 8f on Firm and Standard ground and is lightly raced for its age; last ran just 11 days ago and has no wins in this going profile (0W0P from six runs on similar), with its true hold-up nature masked by appearing in the midfield map.

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding has a strong 14-day rate (11/58) and this 3yo steps up from 7f to 1m — a trip that could suit given the way it has been running; has only run on Standard/Good going and this represents a new challenge over the longer distance, but trainer form makes it interesting.

runners_data.name: Weston Court
runners_data.note: Mapped to the lead despite being a natural hold-up type — the key pace question of the race hinges on whether it can sustain the front-running role it has been pushed into; the visor (headgear) may sharpen it up, but 0W1P from seven runs on similar going and a modest OR of 45 suggest it is fragile in that role.

runners_data.name: Whisper Of Mist
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish flag which is highly relevant if this slow-tempo race produces a sprint finish; three-run form shows finishes of 6th, 11th and 13th, the 63-day absence is the longest in the field, and its true hold-up style is buried further back than the midfield slot implies.

races.paceDynamic: Weston Court is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front from a hold-up profile, meaning this race is likely to be run at a modest, uncontested gallop with no genuine rival to push the tempo. The entire remainder of the field is made up of hold-up types — Mbappe, Thai Princess, Havana Club, Blue Hero, Rival, My Ambition, and Whisper Of Mist — several of whom have been redistributed to midfield simply because there is no room for them all to sit at the back. The field holds far more genuine hold-up horses than the map can place at the rear; Mbappe and Thai Princess are most likely to secure a forward berth within that group given their profiles, but the congestion behind Weston Court is real. With a false-pace scenario highly probable, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly in midfield and produce a sustained late run, rather than those who rely on a true-run test from well off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Holds Up
scenarios.trigger: If Weston Court dictates an uncontested, conservative gallop and the field fails to mount an organised challenge.
scenarios.body: Weston Court sets a falsely-run race from the front, conserving enough energy to repel challengers who have been unable to get into a meaningful rhythm off a slow tempo; horses with positional flexibility to sit just behind the leader benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough for hold-up horses to produce meaningful late runs from a true-run 1m.
scenarios.body: A sustainable but honest gallop allows the better-credentialled hold-up types to close ground through the final two furlongs; those with the highest RPR and proven 1m form on good turf are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Weston Court goes off too hard for a horse of its ability and ties up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A pressured Weston Court weakens sharply inside the final quarter-mile, gifting the race to whichever horse has tracked closest with energy in reserve; short-runners struggle if they have been caught flat-footed by the slow early tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution causes interference or pace confusion in the pack and the race becomes a sprint home.
scenarios.body: With so many horses compressed into the midfield against their natural style, a rough, stop-start race develops and the outcome is determined by luck in running and a late sprint; fitness and draw rather than pure pace profile become decisive.

watchPoints.text: Weston Court is the entire pace foundation of this race — if it fails to hold the lead or capitulates early, the race loses its shape entirely and every scenario probability shifts.
Mbappe carries 140lbs as top weight and has the highest class in the field but the trainer's 0/18 14-day record is a significant red flag — watch for signs of a yard out of form.
Whisper Of Mist's fade-in-finish flag combined with a 63-day layoff makes it a runner to oppose rather than support, especially if the race develops into a sprint finish from a slow pace.
With five horses genuinely redistributed from hold-up into midfield, watch for scrimmaging and traffic issues in the straight — horses on the outer are likely to have the cleanest passage home.
